subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps - Orion Health
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps - Orion Health

Hi Samantha / Carlos -

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we stay aligned while you run the vendor evaluation. High level notes below and a short list of follow-ups.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Long-form clinical note generation: maintaining context over 3k+ token sessions without quality regressions.
- Predictable latency under mixed request sizes (short routing prompts + long synth sessions).
- Cost per inference at scale - unit economics matter for production rollout.
- Data residency and auditability (SOC 2, KMS, SSO).

Decision criteria you described:
1) Latency (p95 and tail for 1k / 3k token sessions)
2) Throughput (sustained concurrent users during peak)
3) Output quality (policy for hallucination / medical correctness)
4) Cost (per-token / per-hour GPU) and autoscaling behavior
5) Security & compliance (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
6) Integration effort (API compatibility, SDKs, SSO)

Competitive bake-off summary from today:
- VendorX: strong latency on short sequences, but no private deployment option and higher per-token cost in our brief tests.
- VendorY: simpler integration but significant quality issues on long-context transcripts we saw in your shared samples.
- Redwood (today's demo): showed consistent generation on 3k sessions in our dev harness, prefix caching reduced token cost in demo scenarios, and we support private deployments + enterprise controls. We'll provide detailed benchmarks and a short trial harness so you can reproduce tests.

Open questions noted on the call:
- Can we reproduce VendorX's latency numbers on your real dataset? (You asked us to run our harness against your sample).
- What are your exact SLA targets for tail latency and RTO for cold starts?
- Procurement timeline and contract/legal redlines you expect in parallel to the bake-off.

Proposed next steps + owners:
- Redwood (Aditya): share product sheet + benchmark workbook and the test harness link by EOD Wed (attached).
- Orion (Samantha / Carlos): share a representative sample dataset (anonymized) and your target SLAs by Fri 11/6.
- Joint: run 48-hour soak test across vendors next week; agree on pass/fail criteria and acceptance window.

Attachments: redwood-product-sheet.pdf (overview), redwood-demo-recording-20261103.mp4 (recording), bench workbook to follow.

If that matches your understanding, I'll queue up the harness and bench run and we can sync briefly after you share the dataset.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps - Orion Health

Thanks Aditya - this looks great and captures the discussion. A couple clarifications and one ask:

Clarifications:
- For decision criteria #1, our target is p95 < 300ms for short prompts and p95 < 1.2s for 3k-token synth sessions under our expected concurrency. Tail (p99) should be reasonable (< 2.5s ideally).
- Cost: we want both per-token and per-inference hour estimates so we can model a 12-month run rate.

Open ask:
- Can Redwood run the harness against a blinded subset of our real clinical notes (we'll anonymize) and produce the same benchmark workbook you mentioned? That will be the primary quantitative input to the procurement team.

Procurement note: procurement@orionhealth.com is looped for timeline visibility. We're aiming to have a preferred vendor decision by end of November if bake-off results are conclusive.

Also, could you confirm whether private deployment (VPC/on-prem) will be available for the POC or if that requires a separate engagement?

Thanks -
Samantha
Head of Clinical Informatics
Orion Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps - Orion Health

Great questions - appreciate the specificity. Short answers and what we're delivering: 

1) Benchmarks: yes - we will run our test harness against the anonymized subset you share. We'll populate the workbook with p50/p95/p99 for the short and long sessions, cost breakdown (per-token, per-hour, autoscaling assumptions), and regression metrics on quality (BLEU/ROUGE and a small clinical correctness checklist). Expect the completed workbook and raw harness results by Thu 11/5 EOD.

2) Private deployment for the POC: we can provide a dedicated VPC-based sandbox for the POC with customer-managed KMS and SSO. For an on-prem full install we'd need a short SOC/security onboarding (can be parallelized). For the bake-off, the VPC sandbox will meet your compliance needs and allow realistic network isolation.

3) Soak test plan: we'll stand up the harness and run 48-hr runs with the following tests:
- Long-context generation (3k tokens) - 2k sessions over 48 hours
- Mixed traffic throughput test (1k concurrent short + 200 concurrent long)
- Cold start tail latency (restart every 6 hours to capture warm/cold behavior)
- Cost simulation under expected traffic profile

Owners & timeline:
- Aditya (Redwood): deliver harness, workbook, and run results - Thu 11/5 EOD.
- Samantha/Carlos (Orion): anonymized dataset + target SLA spreadsheet - Fri 11/6 EOD.
- Joint: kickoff soak test Mon 11/9; review results Wed 11/11.

Attached: redwood-benchmarks-orion-20261104.xlsx (initial draft). Also shared the harness link: https://redwood-test-harness.example.com/orion/run-42 (read-only for now).

Let us know if the timeline is too aggressive and we can adjust.

Best,
Aditya
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@orionhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & next steps - Orion Health

Thanks everyone - that plan and timeline works from my side. Samantha and I will prioritize the anonymized sample and the SLA spreadsheet; procurement is aware of the Fri 11/6 ask.

I'll confirm once the dataset is uploaded to the Drive folder (we'll share the link in a follow-up).

-Carlos
Director, Engineering
Orion Health
